# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 1 | **Condition:** heavily damaged — top of column lost; fragments preserve partial lines

---

**1:1** [...] for-You-are a-God-of-knowledge, and-every-thought of-truth [is] from-You, and-every righteous-purpose [comes] from-before-Your-face [...]

**1:2** [...] without-You nothing is-done, and-nothing is-known without Your-will. There-is-none beside-You, and-there-is-none [...]

**1:3** [...] and-there-is-none to-compare with-Your-glory, and-to-Your-might there-is-no price, and-who among-all Your-great-wondrous-works [...]

**1:4** [...] can-contain Your-glory? And-what-is the-son-of-man among-Your-wondrous-works? And-[one]-born-of-woman, how-shall-he-dwell before-You? [...]

**1:5** [...] he [is] kneaded from-dust, and-the-food-of-worms [is] his-destiny. He [is] pinched-off clay, and-to-dust his-desire returns [...]

**1:6** [...] that-clay might-understand? And-what-can-the-thing-formed-of-dust devise? How-shall-it-direct its-step? [...] and-You-have-established [...]

**1:7** [...] for-Your-glory You-have-done all these-things. [...] a-spirit-of-flesh [...] eternal-council [...]

**1:8** [...] to-walk in-all that-You-love and-to-reject all that-You-hate, and-to-do the-good in-Your-eyes [...]

**1:9** [...] and-You-have-poured-out Your-Holy-Spirit upon-Your-servant [...] to-purify-him from-all deeds-of-wickedness [...]

**1:10** [...] in-the-abundance-of Your-compassions and-in-the-multitude-of Your-mercies to-all the-sons-of Your-truth [...]

**1:11** [...] You-have-opened a-fountain for-the-cleansing-of the-unclean-one [...] and a-pool-of-purification for-the-guilty [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 1 of 1QHa is heavily damaged. The top several lines are entirely lost. What survives from approximately lines 1-11 shows fragments of a hymn praising God's omniscience and sovereignty, followed by a meditation on human frailty ("kneaded from dust," "food of worms") and God's purifying grace through the Holy Spirit. The clay/dust anthropology and the spirit-flesh dualism are characteristic Qumran themes. [...] marks genuine lacunae where the manuscript is physically damaged or missing. Bracketed words [like this] are scholarly reconstructions based on parallel passages in 1QHa and 1QS.*

— EMET
